public_rationale: Marcus rejected Musk's April 2024 forecast that AI smarter than any one human would arrive around the end of 2025. The deadline has passed. The ARC Prize organisers' report on 2025 says every ARC-AGI-2 task was solved by ordinary untrained people. The best 2025 competition entry scored 24%, and the organisers wrote that 'we have not yet achieved AGI.' In January 2026, Musk himself said AI smarter than any human 'might' come by the end of 2026 or in 2027, which treats it as not yet here. AI did reach gold-medal level at the 2025 math olympiad, but that is one narrow area and does not show it was smarter than every human in general. The forecast that such AI would not arrive by end of 2025 holds.
limitations: There is no formal test for 'smarter than any one human'. The judgment uses a plain reading of general cognitive ability.
The Musk evidence comes from a news report, not a primary transcript.
Benchmarks measure only parts of intelligence.

post title: we won't see human-superior AGI by the end of 2025
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that no AI system will be smarter than any single human by 31 December 2025, meaning better than every individual person across general cognitive ability, not just in narrow areas.
Doing better than humans on some narrow tasks or benchmarks (such as math contests) does not count as 'smarter than any one human'. The test is general ability.

The deadline is the end of 2025, as the post title says. 'Around the end of next year' could stretch a little past that, but Musk's own January 2026 remarks put the event still in the future, so the result is the same either way.
criteria.support_condition: Through 31 December 2025, no AI system was broadly recognised as smarter than every individual human. Independent general-reasoning evaluations still show tasks that ordinary humans solve and AI cannot, or credible observers (including the forecaster) say such AI has not arrived yet.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible independent evaluations or broad expert recognition show that an AI system available by 31 December 2025 beat every individual human across general cognitive tasks.

evidence.excerpt: By this definition, we have not yet achieved AGI.
evidence.publisher: arXiv (ARC Prize Foundation: Chollet, Knoop, Kamradt, Landers)
evidence.explanation: The benchmark organisers judged that as of the end of the 2025 competition cycle there were still tasks easy for ordinary humans but hard for AI, so AGI had not been reached. That is consistent with no AI being smarter than every human by end of 2025.

evidence.excerpt: The top competition score reached a new state-of-the-art on the ARC-AGI-2 private dataset of 24% at a compute cost of $0.20 per task.
evidence.explanation: The same report says every ARC-AGI-2 task was solved by at least two untrained members of the public. The best 2025 competition entry scored 24% on the private set, so AI did not exceed every human on this general-reasoning test.

evidence.explanation: At Davos in January 2026, the person who made the original forecast still described AI smarter than any human as a future event (end of 2026 or 2027). This implies it had not arrived by the end of 2025.

evidence.excerpt: achieved gold medal performance at the 2025 International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO), solving five out of six brutally difficult problems and earning 35 out of 42 possible points.
evidence.explanation: Shows that AI matched elite humans in one narrow area in 2025. It solved five of six problems, which is not proof that it beat every human in general ability. It is listed as the strongest counterpoint.
